changes.from:
Make ctx the shared owner of context bundle format, storage, artifact management, OCR, and portable .ctx export for Omni Agent Handoff and future tools.

Design decisions:
- Bundle storage is central and app-independent, e.g. XDG data under ctx bundles, not inside Omni repos.
- Bundle id format: timestamp + short id + optional slug, e.g. 2026-06-24T10-41-03Z_7hf3k2_build-slides.
- Bundle lifecycle: draft -> sent -> archived/cancelled; collection creates draft immediately.
- Bundle item schema includes image, text, file, url, desktop_snapshot, handoff_record.
- .ctx archive is zipped portable form for remote/Oqto upload.
- File items support copied and referenced storage; target/export decides whether references must be materialized.
- OCR belongs in ctx; v1 can shell out to `ocrs` CLI as backend.

Acceptance / proof:
- ctx can create a bundle, add images/text/files/URLs/snapshots, run OCR for an image, export .ctx, and render agent-readable context.md.
- Schemas are generated/synced to ~/byteowlz/schemas.
- Existing ctx capture behavior continues to work.
- `cargo check` and relevant tests pass.

changes.from:
## Outcome

Enable a person to deliberately send or stage a reviewed  Bundle, with an optional instruction, to an external destination without coupling ctx-core to Oqto or any other agent host. ctx owns capture, Bundle review/export, neutral handoff values, and a small destination seam. Each integration owns authentication, target discovery, upload, prompt/message semantics, and target-specific identifiers. Start with the simplest sufficient API; MCP remains an optional resource/pull surface through ctx-mcp, not a required transport for push handoff.

## Domain constraints

- Current Context is lightweight device-local state and MUST NOT trigger network calls, uploads, prompt submission, or model-context injection.
- Only an explicit user action may create a Handoff from a reviewed Bundle.
- Target identifiers and remote references are opaque to ctx; no Oqto Account, Session, work-directory, Runner, placement, or other target-domain types enter ctx-core.
- A Handoff distinguishes at least  and  modes when the destination supports them, and unsupported modes fail explicitly.
- Destination implementations may use a simple HTTP API, an existing SDK/CLI, MCP, or another transport; the domain contract must not require one. Do not invent a new wire protocol or adapter framework until a concrete second implementation proves the need.
- Credentials remain owned by the destination integration and must not be persisted in Bundle manifests or receipts.

## Candidate neutral values

- : opaque id/URI plus human-readable title/description.
- : request/idempotency id, pinned Bundle id/hash/archive, optional instruction, opaque target, requested mode, and source provenance.
- : staged/sent/rejected status, opaque remote references, target display data, warnings, and retry-safe correlation.
- A minimal destination interface should be explored around  and ; keep it deep and avoid leaking target-specific methods.

## UX requirements

- CLI/Overlay flow is Capture/choose existing Bundle -> review/redact -> choose destination/target -> add instruction -> stage/send -> show receipt.
- cwd/project/app/URL from Current Context may be passed as neutral target-suggestion hints. Ambiguous resolution MUST present choices or fail; never silently guess.
- Preview is the default. Noninteractive confirmation is allowed only through an explicit flag and must remain auditable.
- Offline, unauthorized, oversized, unsupported-content, duplicate/retry, and ambiguous-target outcomes are legible and preserve the local Bundle.

## Proof of positive outcome

1. Unit/schema tests round-trip neutral targets, requests, receipts, modes, opaque references, provenance, and structured errors.
2. A fake destination proves ctx-core has no dependency on any product integration and demonstrates target discovery plus stage/send receipts.
3. A CLI integration test sends a self-contained test Bundle through the seam after explicit confirmation and prints stable JSON receipt output.
4. Tests prove , focus reports, screenshot watching, and Bundle creation alone perform no handoff/network/model action.
5. Retrying with the same idempotency identity does not create an unbounded duplicate handoff in the fake implementation.
6. Ambiguous target hints return explicit choices; unavailable/denied targets never fall back to another destination.
7. Bundle consent/redaction rules for clipboard, selections, screenshots, page text, and local paths survive handoff unchanged.
8. A conformance fixture is sufficient for an external repository to implement an Oqto or other destination without importing target concepts into ctx-core.

## Boundaries

- No Oqto implementation in this issue; track that in Oqto.
- No automatic context injection or ambient event-driven sends.
- No requirement to expose ctx-mcp publicly or make device-local resources remotely reachable.
- No package registry or generalized plugin runtime.
- Do not replace  archive export, which remains the universal manual fallback.

Split implementation children only after the neutral contract and first real destination reveal actual seams.

## Candidate neutral values

- `DestinationTarget`: opaque id/URI plus human-readable title/description.
- `HandoffRequest`: request/idempotency id, pinned Bundle id/hash/archive, optional instruction, opaque target, requested mode, and source provenance.
- `HandoffReceipt`: staged/sent/rejected status, opaque remote references, target display data, warnings, and retry-safe correlation.

## UX requirements

- CLI/Overlay flow is Capture/choose existing Bundle -> review/redact -> choose destination/target -> add instruction -> stage/send -> show receipt.

## Proof of positive outcome

1. Unit/schema tests round-trip neutral targets, requests, receipts, modes, opaque references, provenance, and structured errors.
2. A fake destination proves ctx-core has no dependency on any product integration and demonstrates target discovery plus stage/send receipts.
3. A CLI integration test sends a self-contained test Bundle through the seam after explicit confirmation and prints stable JSON receipt output.
4. Tests prove `ctx current`, focus reports, screenshot watching, and Bundle creation alone perform no handoff/network/model action.
5. Retrying with the same idempotency identity does not create an unbounded duplicate handoff in the fake implementation.
6. Ambiguous target hints return explicit choices; unavailable/denied targets never fall back to another destination.
7. Bundle consent/redaction rules for clipboard, selections, screenshots, page text, and local paths survive handoff unchanged.
8. A conformance fixture is sufficient for an external repository to implement an Oqto or other destination without importing target concepts into ctx-core.

## Boundaries

- No Oqto implementation in this issue; track that in Oqto.
